title: How repo-video works
description: A four-scene example: what the skill makes, its four build stages, how a scene marks what appears and what lights up, and a real build.

scenes.title: What it makes
steps: This is repo-video, a skill that turns a repository or a pull request into a narrated explainer.
Each scene reveals its items one by one, and highlights the one the voice is talking about.
The result is an MP4 with captions, on a page with chapters and a transcript.

scenes.title: Four stages
steps: One command builds the video. It runs four stages, in order.
First, speech. Every step's narration becomes a sound file, cached, so an edit only re-records what changed.
Then render. Chromium plays each step's animation, and the script captures it frame by frame.
Assemble joins the frames and the narration with ffmpeg, so every picture lasts exactly as long as its sentence.
Finally, page writes the video page, ready to publish.

scenes.title: A scene
steps: A scene is one HTML file, nineteen twenty by ten eighty.
data-step says when an item appears. It is highlighted at that step, and dims afterwards.
data-focus highlights an item again later: here, a single line of code.
And data-emph none keeps a container out of the highlight, so only its lines light up.

scenes.title: A real build
steps: Here is the real output of building this example with the default macOS voice.
Narration and frames for all fifteen steps, scene by scene.
And the finished video, with its length and size, ready for the page.
